fact: The report says the police information system launched by the Director General of National Security on 19 June 2025 is meant to digitise the work of police commissariats and to document, among other things, the reports and complaints made at commissariats and their offices.

The report says the system was put to work on 19 June 2025 for, among others, central commissioners and heads of judicial police sections in the commissariats, who register in a database held by the central office for collecting police information, to which police centres are being linked.

The director of the central office gave the stages of linking as 27 National Police centres and 7 National Gendarmerie centres (plus 2 customs centres, not counted here), with no total of stations; the report separately puts the rollout across Nouakchott's commissariats at 90 per cent complete.

The report says the programme is supervised by the central office for collecting police information in the judicial police directorate of the General Directorate of National Security, whose Director General launched it on 19 June 2025.

On 19 June 2025 the Director General of National Security launched work with the WAPIS police information system for central directors, the regional directors of the Nouakchott wilayas, central commissioners and heads of judicial police sections in the commissariats.
